newsitem.title: BELGIUM: INSIGHT-CHARTISTS MOSTLY NEUTRAL ON BEL-20.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-CHARTISTS MOSTLY NEUTRAL ON BEL-20.

text.p: Belgian analysts were mostly
neutral about the trend of the Bel-20 share index after a week
of consolidation.
The Bel-20 ended at 1,773.35 on Friday compared with
1,794.11 on October 4, and well down from October 3's record

Contributors' own analysis:
CERA - On the one hand Belgian economic growth accelerated
in the second quarter; on the other hand investors focus on
whether the Fed will raise rates... For us, both are signs to
shift from interest sensitive stocks to cyclicals. For the
Bel-20, we believe Belgian shares are likely to track other
European markets in the coming days. A first resistance is the
psycholigically important level of 1,800, a second is at the
last high of 1,829. At 1,750 and 1,700 there are technical
support levels -- Guy Sips.
BANK DEGROOF - The market managed to close above the 1,765
level which has now become for us the "turning point". Only a
close below this heavy support would allow a more pronounced
correction. As a matter of fact, as long as interest rates stay
so low and the dollar so strong, we see no fundamental reason
for a severe downturn. On the other hand, the upside is capped
at the 1,795-1,805 level without new incentives -- Joel
Crevecoeur.
ECOFIS - The long black of last Monday closed the bullish
window or gap at 1,780-84 made between Oct 1 and 2, and this set
the downward tone for the week. On the weekly chart a small
two-bar reversal (and dark cloud cover in candlestick jargon)
was produced, which together with the stochastics points to the
likelihood of a pause to down-reversal. But in the daily chart a
small bullish engulfing pattern occured last Friday. Together
with the daily stochastics, this could entail a pause to
up-reversal. These opposing technicals could make the Bel-20
move sideways this week -- Frank Boll.
GENERALE BANK - The fall back after last week's record chase
was dramatic. The Bel-20 index completely lost its upward
momentum and drifted systematically lower in moderate turnover.
On Friday the negative sentiment turned positive, though only by
a rally at the close. Trading tools show first signs of
bottoming out, but we would prefer some confirmation before
changing our neutral stance. The index has been consolidating
around these levels for the last week now. A revisiting of the
1,740 level and (even worse) a loss of it would be a bearish
signal -- Geert Vanderbeke.
